newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - hangs on India tender.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - hangs on India tender.

text.p: Gulf middle distillate markets are eagerly waiting for Indian Oil Corp (IOC) to award its September high speed diesel tender which traders expect will disappoint sellers struggling in a well-supplied market.
Gulf traders on Thursday said they expected IOC to award less than 250,000 tonnes in the tender as monsoon rains in the country reduced agricultural fuel demand.
Further pressure on the market is expected if Iraq resumes crude exports from its Mina al-Bakr terminal under Baghdad's "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations by early August.
"IOC won't buy anything close to the 800,000 to one million tonnes of diesel it bought earlier in the year," said one trader resident in the Gulf.
The IOC tender seeks 0.5 percent sulphur diesel for deliveries to Madras or Haldia on the east coast and 1.0-percent grade to the east coast and to Kandla on the west coast.
Bids for the tender are valid until August 1 and details of the award is expected to emerge on Monday.
Without major buying from IOC, traders expected a steady improvement in premiums to be quickly capped.

Diesel premiums to price quotes were talked at 20-30 cents with a prompt Kuwaiti cargo said sold at plus 40 cents. Kerosene cargoes stuck at a slight discount to the quote but was talked at plus 10-15 cents for September cargoes.
Demand into east Africa, as Gulf prices fell below Mediterranean levels, was also mildly supportive to the market.
Trader demand for Indonesian requirements has also been behind a gradual improvement in the middle of the barrel.
Outright prices improved over the week with gas oil assessed at $21 a barrel fob Gulf on Thursday and jet at $21.10.
Despite the rise and the return of gas oil's premium over jet, prices remain close to year-lows.

Fuel oil markets have firmed on crude's rise, reaching $91 a tonne on Thursday, its highest level since March. The discount to quotes narrowed to around $2 a tonne while 380-cst Fujairah 380-cst bunkers have moved up $2 to $98-100 a tonne.
Naphtha prices have been pushed to $193 a tonne its strongest since middle June on rising crude and gasoline.
Tenders from state refiners in the region were thin though traders expected Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) to return to the market offering jet or diesel.
A 30-day maintenance shutdown at Saudi Aramco's Ras Tanura refinery was expected to start in the second half of August but traders said the impact on product supplies would be minimal.
